reason: Moses is unambiguously portrayed as an established national leader exercising authoritative command. He positions himself at the gate of the camp (a position of authority and decision-making), issues a public call for loyalty ('Who is on the Lord's side?'), and the entire assembly of Levites gathers to him. He then delivers binding military and religious orders that are immediately obeyed ('And the sons of Levi did as Moses said'). He speaks with divine authority ('Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel'), makes consequential decisions affecting the entire nation, executes judgment through the Levites, and pronounces blessings. All of this demonstrates Moses functioning as an established national leader rather than an aspiring one.
